title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous pages): Σ is the Riemann sphere P^1(C) with the three real marked points J = {0,1,∞} = {R_0,R_1,R_∞} on the real circle Σ_R. Σ̃ → Σ is the real oriented blow-up at the points of J. Each R_i is replaced by its circle U_i of real tangent directions, so Σ̃ is a pair of pants whose boundary is the union of the U_i, and Σ* = Σ∖J is its interior. The group Γ acts on the whole situation; it is S_3 (the automorphisms of (P^1,J)) times complex conjugation τ, of order 12. Grothendieck wants a system of base points on Σ̃ that is stable under Γ, so that he can write down a Γ-equivariant presentation of the fundamental groupoid Π_1(Σ̃).

On this page he introduces four families of base points (16), drawn in the figure as a round sphere. The three R_i sit symmetrically on the equator Σ_R and the poles are P^±.

(i) Q_i, the antipode of R_i on Σ_R. In the S_3-symmetric metric these are the real fixed points of the three involutions: Q_0 = 2, Q_1 = -1, Q_∞ = 1/2.

(ii) P_ε, for ε ∈ π_0(Σ∖Σ_R), i.e. ε indexes the two hemispheres. By (17), P_ε is the unique point of Δ lying in hemisphere ε. Here Δ is presumably the fixed locus of the 3-cycles, so P^± = e^{±iπ/3}, the two 'j=0' points.

(iii) R_i^ω ∈ U_i, the two real tangent directions at R_i. (18) gives a canonical bijection U_{iR} := U_i ∩ T_{Σ_R,R_i} ≅ ω, where ω is the set of the two orientations of Σ_R: a direction along Σ_R at R_i determines an orientation of the circle. ω is also identified with the two cyclic orders on J.

(iv) S_i^ε, the two tangent directions at R_i along the great circle Σ_i through P^+, P^- and Q_i (the meridian through R_i). By (19), these are indexed by ε, because the two directions point into the two hemispheres. The marginal NB suggests writing Σ̃_ε for the two closed half-pants, with S_i^ε ∈ Σ̃_ε.

This gives 3 + 2 + 6 + 6 = 17 base points. Γ permutes each family transitively; τ fixes the Q_i and R_i^ω and swaps the ε-indices. The bottom of the page notes that ω ≅ {±1} via cyclic permutations ('+' = the circular permutation, '-' = its inverse). Once an orientation of Σ is chosen one also gets ε ≅ {±1}: the hemisphere whose boundary orientation is the given one.

The crossed-out lines (a_i^ω, b_i, c_i^ω, 'relations pythagoriques'?) anticipate page 50. There the paths a (along U_i), b (along Σ̃_R), c (from P to Q along great circles) and d (from P to S) are defined. Each family is a torsor under the symmetry group, and they form a symmetric generating system of the groupoid. The figure already labels all these arcs. The aim is a Γ-equivariant description of the profinite fundamental groupoid of P^1∖{0,1,∞} with tangential base points, as the base case of the Galois action on the Teichmüller tower.
errors: No mathematical errors. The equivalence ω ≅ ε holds only after fixing an orientation of Σ, and that orientation is reversed by τ; Grothendieck states this condition himself.
The text says Σ_i is determined by P_ε and Q_i, but it is the great circle through R_i (and Q_i) and the poles. This is consistent, since Q_i is antipodal to R_i.

ideas.what: Real oriented blow-up of P^1 at 0,1,∞; points of the boundary circles used as base points (tangential base points)
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points / real oriented blow-up (Kato–Nakayama log space)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne 1989 (tangential base points); Kato–Nakayama 1999 for log Betti spaces
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) mentions tangential base points and the 'Lego' of Teichmüller groupoids

ideas.what: A fully S_3×Z/2-symmetric set of base points: the j=0 points e^{±iπ/3}, the real fixed points -1, 1/2, 2, and 12 tangential directions (real ones and ones along the meridians)
ideas.modern_name: Symmetric base point systems for the GT action (e.g. the six tangential base points and the 'ρ' base points)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse discusses a base-point-orbit philosophy for Teichmüller groupoids but not this explicit set

ideas.what: Identification of real tangent directions at R_i with orientations of Σ_R, i.e. with the cyclic orders on J
ideas.modern_name: Torsor bookkeeping of tangential base points

missed.claim: The page builds an explicit Γ = S_3×⟨τ⟩-equivariant system of 17 base points on the real blow-up of P^1∖{0,1,∞}. These include tangential base points along the meridians (S_i^ε), not only the real ones. Together with the path families a, b, c, d of page 50, this is a cellular, equivariant presentation of the fundamental groupoid. It predates the GT literature's use of the 01/10 tangential base points and Nakamura's meridian-type base points, so it is a precursor rather than an unknown result.
missed.quote: S_i^ε ∈ U_i∩TΣ_i = TU_{Σ_i} ... on a TU_{Σ_i} ≃ ε car les deux directions tangentes à Σ_i en R_i se distinguent suivant les deux hémisphères
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority: it shows Grothendieck around 1978+ already using tangential base points and an equivariant cellular decomposition of the pants. Comparable material appears later in Ihara, Drinfeld and Nakamura–Schneps.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an early, explicit use of the real oriented blow-up with tangential base points and a fully symmetric base point system, before Deligne's 1989 formalisation. The underlying mathematics is now standard and partly announced in the Esquisse; its main value is as evidence of early date and method.
transcription_corrections: (16) third line: 'P_ε (ε ∈ ε = π_0(Σ∖Σ_R))', with the 'en' crossed out.
In the margin note to (19), Σ_i is described as 'le grand cercle déterminé par les P_ε et Q_i'. It should be read as the great circle (meridian) through the poles and Q_i.

Main text read as: 'Σ_R étant une variété de dim 1, l'une des orientations de celle-ci aux points R_i (donc globalement) est en correspondance biunivoque avec l'une des deux directions orientées tangentes.'
Marginal NB: 'Il faudrait introduire Σ̃_ε (ε∈ε), les deux hémisphères sur Σ̃; le choix des S_i^ε est symbolisé par S_i^ε ∈ Σ̃_ε'.
Bottom: 'et en choisissant une orientation sur Σ, ω ≃ {+1,-1}, d'où ε ≃ {+1,-1}'.
Crossed-out phrase is likely 'relations pythagoriques' or similar; the reading is uncertain.
